subject: Mobile Development
title: How the GPS in Your Phone Works
description: A 60-second lesson on How the GPS in Your Phone Works.

hook.text: Your phone knows where you are within three meters. It uses satellites in orbit.

buildup.text: GPS receivers listen to signals from at least four satellites to triangulate your position.

discovery.text: Phones also use cell towers and Wi-Fi networks to speed up location fixes.

twist.text: GPS is power-hungry. A navigation app can drain 20% of your battery in one hour.

climax.text: Location services power maps, ride-sharing, weather, and fitness — all enabled by GPS chips.

punchline.text: Four satellites tell your phone where you stand.

quiz.question: How many GPS satellites are needed for a position fix?
